raw_response:
I will keep all 6.0 mu in stevia this year. I am experienced, the plot is small, and my household labor is limited because some family members work off-farm, so I will choose a management plan that is stable and controllable rather than complicated. Since I have well irrigation at the start of the season, I will rely on improved seedling material to keep stand establishment uniform and reduce risk. I will use rotary tillage because it is efficient for a small stevia field and gives me a fine seedbed without as much labor as deep ploughing. For fertilizer, I will stay with a moderate, balanced program: enough nitrogen to support leaf growth, but not so much that quality becomes unstable; phosphorus for root establishment early; potassium to support leaf yield and stress tolerance. Because I can irrigate from a well, I will schedule several irrigations through the season to avoid drought stress, especially after establishment and during strong vegetative growth. I will also plan several pesticide applications because stevia leaf production depends on keeping foliage clean and marketable. My goal is steady management, good leaf yield, and low operational risk on a 6.0 mu farm that I can manage confidently myself.
